nodes.label: supermux (mobile-first agentic development environment)
nodes.rationale: Coding agents do their best work in long-running sessions; a laptop lid, a commute, or one unanswered question should not stop them. Self-hosted on hardware the user controls so subscriptions, repositories and credentials stay with the user and no supermux account is required.

nodes.label: supermux broker (source of truth)
nodes.rationale: The broker runs on the host, supervises agent sessions, keeps histories, routes messages and exposes workspace APIs. Control operations happen in the broker specifically so switching or inspecting sessions does not spend agent tokens.

nodes.label: Built-in connectivity relay (relay.supermux.dev)
nodes.rationale: Enabled by default on native CLI/desktop hosts so each host gets a stable HTTPS address without opening a router port or configuring a tunnel. Trade-off explicitly stated: relay traffic is encrypted in transit but not yet end-to-end encrypted at the application layer; `--no-relay` keeps a host LAN-only.

nodes.label: Pairing, not accounts
nodes.rationale: New devices join with a short-lived, single-use claim bound to the host identity instead of a hosted account, so a client can hold several independently owned hosts in one fleet and no central identity provider is required.

nodes.label: Per-worker isolated git worktree
nodes.rationale: Every worker gets its own worktree so the main checkout only moves through an explicit finish action (merge locally, open a PR, keep the branch, or discard). Review happens before anything lands.

nodes.label: Pluggable agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode)
nodes.rationale: All four share the same workflow so model or reasoning settings can change without starting over; the user picks whichever subscription they actually own.

nodes.label: Optional personal-assistant (PA) session
nodes.rationale: Fresh installs deliberately do NOT create a PA — normal project sessions are the default workflow; an always-on orchestrator is opt-in from Settings.

nodes.label: Environment configuration (MUX_* variables)
nodes.rationale: Native installs read ~/.mux/state/.env; Docker reads .env in the project directory — one variable surface across both deployment paths.
